4.6 TIMEKEEPING PROCEDURE (CURRENT, AS REVISED APRIL 2018)

Staff should record their arrival and departure times on the weekly timesheet
kept in the front office. The timesheet is divided into columns for each day of
the week, with a separate column for the total hours worked. Overtime should be
recorded in the remarks column, together with a brief note of the reason. The
office manager checks the timesheet at the end of each week and initials it
before passing it to the partners for approval.

The following rules apply to the calculation of hours:

- The normal working day is 7.5 hours, excluding the one-hour lunch break.
- Time worked in excess of 7.5 hours in a day is recorded as overtime.
- Overtime is paid at time-and-a-half for the first two hours, and double time
  thereafter.
- Time worked on a Saturday is paid at time-and-a-half. Time worked on a
  Sunday or a bank holiday is paid at double time.
- No overtime is payable for time worked at home unless the work has been
  authorised in advance by a partner.

4.6 TIMEKEEPING PROCEDURE (CURRENT, AS REVISED APRIL 2018)

Staff should record their arrival and departure times on the weekly timesheet
kept in the front office. The timesheet is divided into columns for each day of

recorded in the remarks column, together with a brief note of the reason. The
